paragraphs: The Pharos of Alexandria stood for well over a thousand years and then fell to earthquakes, leaving no ruin to photograph and no drawing made from life. Every image of it is a reconstruction from coins, descriptions and the shape of its foundations: a square base, an octagonal middle, a round tower with a fire at the top.
The model holds 170,985 polygons and 207,988 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $189 it suits historical and educational visualisation, museum and exhibition work, documentary and film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

Almost everyone in medieval Europe was a peasant, and almost every medieval scene gets built around the few who were not. A plain tunic, a belt, working hands: this is the figure that fills a village, a market or a field, and without him a castle scene looks staged.

The character runs 19,853 polygons and 19,021 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, deliberately light so it can be used in crowds. It ships rigged, and the same character is also offered in an eating pose on a separate listing.

At $189 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits game crowds and villages, historical visualisation, film and television previsualisation, education and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Ultra large container ships are the biggest moving objects humans build. They are too large for the Panama Canal, too deep for most ports, and their economics only work because a single voyage carries what once took a fleet. Seen alongside a tug, the scale stops being an abstraction.

The hull carries 749,740 polygons and 856,469 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and holds StemCell certification. Related vessels sit alongside it in the library, including the OOCL Hong Kong versions and a general heavy freight build.
At $189 it suits logistics and shipping visualisation, port and infrastructure scenes, documentary and news graphics, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Infants are hard to model and harder to buy: proportions that no adult scan can be shrunk into, a bodysuit rather than clothing, and a sitting pose that is one of the few a baby holds on their own. This figure exists because family, healthcare and childcare scenes need it and rarely have it.
The model holds 37,460 polygons and 70,835 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in a static seated pose. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $179 it suits family and lifestyle visualisation, healthcare and childcare material, advertising and product context, interior renders and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The A400M is the odd one out among modern military transports: turboprops rather than jets, chosen so it can lift heavy loads off short and rough strips that a jet would never attempt. Those eight bladed scimitar propellers are the aircraft's signature, and they turn in opposite directions on each wing.

The airframe holds 245,953 polygons and 257,119 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps, 7 at 8192x8192 and 6 at 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification. The library also holds the green scheme and rigged builds, including native rigs for Maya and Cinema 4D.
At $179 it suits flight simulation, aviation and defence visualisation, documentary and film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

A bald eagle at full spread is almost all wing, and the wide pose is the one everybody pictures: primaries fanned, head turned, the moment before or after a stoop. It is also the hardest pose to fake, because the feather layering changes shape completely once the wing opens.
This build is prepared for Blender and ships rigged, so the wings and body can be posed or animated inside the native scene rather than rebuilt after import. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $179 it suits wildlife documentary and education, national and patriotic imagery, game and film assets, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

High visibility orange and a hardhat are less a uniform than a legal requirement, which is why the same silhouette appears on sites and plant floors everywhere. For a render it does a specific job: it gives scale to machinery and tells the viewer instantly that the scene is a workplace.

The figure holds 52,412 polygons and 53,725 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 25 maps, 18 at 4096x4096, 6 at 2048x2048 and one at 512x512. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification and is supplied in a standing pose.
At $179 it suits industrial and construction visualisation, safety and training material, equipment marketing, architectural scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

A studio figure is posed for the camera rather than for life: weight shifted, shoulders squared, expression held. That is exactly what garment and campaign work needs, because the pose is the one the photographer would have asked for anyway.
The model holds 167,913 polygons and 173,929 vertices in quads and tris, with mixed UV layout across the parts. It is a static figure, built to CheckMate specification.
At $179 it suits fashion and garment visualisation, advertising and campaign mockups, retail and e-commerce imagery, editorial illustration and film previsualisation. On sale since 2025.

Marmon built trucks for owner operators, which is why so many were specified with chrome, long hoods and custom trim rather than fleet plainness. Paired with a Sun Valley car carrier trailer, it becomes the machine that delivers new cars to dealerships, a familiar sight on any interstate.

The model is dense, 1,855,081 polygons over 982,336 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering both the tractor and the multi level carrier deck. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $179 it suits transport and logistics visualisation, automotive marketing, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

The mounted T-rex is a piece of museum design as much as palaeontology. The skeleton is posed, braced and lit to be walked around, and generations of visitors know the animal by that mount rather than by any reconstruction of its flesh.
This build is prepared for Blender, so it opens as a native scene rather than an import, and is supplied as a static mount. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $179 it suits museum and exhibition work, palaeontology and science education, documentary and film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The AW101 is the helicopter countries buy when the weather is the enemy. Norway operates it for search and rescue along a coast where the sea state and the darkness are the real hazard, and the aircraft is sized around carrying a full medical team out and a rescue load back.

The model is built at subdivision level, 247,089 polygons and 258,076 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, and holds CheckMate Lite and Pro certification. The Royal Air Force Merlin scheme is offered as a separate listing.
At $169 it suits search and rescue visualisation, defence and aviation presentation, documentary and film, flight simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The carousel is the oldest ride still running in most parks, and the one least changed. Carved horses on brass poles, a mirrored centre drum, a canopy of lights: it survives because nobody has found a way to improve on it that visitors actually wanted.

The model is built at subdivision level, 513,512 polygons and 505,276 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, covering the platform, the mounts and the canopy. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build for animating the rotation is offered separately.
At $169 it suits amusement park and leisure visualisation, architectural and urban scenes, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

Most anatomy models stop at muscle, which is where the interesting problems begin for vascular medicine. Showing the veins and the subcutaneous fat layer together explains varicose disease, injection sites and swelling in a way a muscle map cannot, because those conditions live in the tissue above the muscle.
The model holds 114,776 polygons and 115,070 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the right leg with its venous and fat layers. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $169 it suits medical education and patient explanation, vascular and phlebology material, nursing training, pharmaceutical visualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The C-17 with its ramp down is the image of military logistics: an aircraft that can put a tank on an unpaved strip and back itself out again afterwards. The open cargo door is the whole point of the design, and a closed airframe hides what makes the type unusual.

The model holds 1,380,711 polygons and 1,468,755 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the cargo door modelled open. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification. The library also holds the closed airframe, an in flight build, and rigged versions including native rigs for Maya and Cinema 4D.
At $169 it suits defence and logistics visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.
